newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Act NZ's Prebble to announce caucus decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Act NZ's Prebble to announce caucus decision soon.

text.p: Act New Zealand leader Richard Prebble said on Wednesday he hopes to make an announcement today on his party's support for the new centre-right coalition government.
Prebble told Radio New Zealand Act's caucus had worked its way through most of the issues after meeting for most of Tuesday.

"I think the caucus has actually reached a unanimous view but it's a very serious one, so what we've actually done is we've sent out to the board...the view that we've reached, and we're getting feedback from them.
"We're collating that information this morning and if it turns out to be unanimous, and I think it's going to be, I might be able to make a statement today," Prebble said.
"It's going to be a fairly long one. It's going to set out our reservations and the views that we take and the principle that we intend to adopt."
Act is concerned about spending promises and civil rights issues in the coalition document.
Prebble said Act was also worried about news media reports that the National-NZ First coalition document contained some secret agreements.

"There's confusion because while (NZ First leader and deputy Prime Minister) Mr Peters says yes, there are, that hasn't been confirmed by the Prime Minister, and we're quite concerned about the nature of those secret agreements," Prebble said.
He said it was almost certain that at some stage over the three year parliamentary term the new government would need Act's support.

There had been no explanation from Winston Peters why several of his party's top candidates had been passed over for ministerial positions, but it was well known that those candidates favoured a coalition with Labour.

"It may well be...that two of them might walk, and if that happens, the government will fall without Act. Now we don't want to make a snap decision then -- we want to have a careful look at the issues now.
"It also appears to us that the government itself may not have made up its mind totally on a number of matters, and we want to indicate to them very clearly what Act's view is.
"If we can talk them out of undermining our basic civil rights, I think Act will have justified its presence just on that alone," Prebble said.
He ruled out the possibility of formally joining the new coalition government.
"No way. We're only going to vote for them on confidence issues. There is no way in the world I am going to vote for that socialist nonsense in health. It's throwing away money."
